criteria.description: When fetch rejects inside toggleFavourite, the catch block must call setFavouriteIds with a functional updater that undoes the optimistic change: if wasAdded === true, removes productId; if wasAdded === false, adds productId back.
criteria.evidence: Code inspection of FavouritesContext.tsx lines 79-88: catch block contains `setFavouriteIds((prev) => { const next = new Set(prev); if (wasAdded) { next.delete(productId); } else { next.add(productId); } return next; });` — exactly matches the required functional-updater revert pattern using wasAdded.

criteria.description: The revert in the catch block must use a functional state updater (setFavouriteIds(prev => ...)) rather than closing over the pre-toggle favouriteIds snapshot.
criteria.evidence: Code inspection of FavouritesContext.tsx line 80: catch block calls `setFavouriteIds((prev) => { ... })` — a callback/functional updater, not a captured Set literal. Only `wasAdded` (a boolean captured synchronously) is closed over; the `favouriteIds` Set itself is never captured.

criteria.description: Before the fetch call, setPendingIds must be called to add productId to pendingIds, making isPending(productId) return true during the request.
criteria.evidence: Code inspection of FavouritesContext.tsx lines 61-65: `setPendingIds((prev) => { const next = new Set(prev); next.add(productId); return next; });` appears before the `try` block at line 67 (which contains the await fetch calls) — outside any try block, before fetch is called.

criteria.description: After the fetch settles (success or failure), setPendingIds must be called in a finally block to remove productId from pendingIds.
criteria.evidence: Code inspection of FavouritesContext.tsx lines 90-95: `finally { setPendingIds((prev) => { const next = new Set(prev); next.delete(productId); return next; }); }` — cleanup is exclusively in a finally block, not duplicated in try or catch.
